proposed_comments.title: Complete PowerDisplay compatibility validation
proposed_comments.body:
### Complete PowerDisplay compatibility validation

**Severity:** `medium`

Thanks for adding the demo and validation details. Before this can move forward, please also test the new Follow Screen Brightness mode with PowerDisplay profile switching enabled for both light and dark profiles, as requested in the thread. The important thing to confirm is that brightness changes caused by applying a PowerDisplay profile do not create a repeated light/dark feedback loop.

confidence.rationale: A maintainer explicitly requested this compatibility test, and the feature shares LightSwitch theme notifications with PowerDisplay profile application.

proposed_comments.title: Bound shutdown when WMI is unavailable

confidence.rationale: The worker performs synchronous WMI calls and Stop joins that worker; the proposed pattern was built in the fork service project.

proposed_comments.title: Use a deterministic value when multiple built-in panels report brightness

confidence.rationale: The WMI class can return multiple rows and the current implementation requests one row; maximum aggregation is a simple deterministic policy but product may choose a different one.

proposed_comments.title: Invalidate cached brightness when no active panel is reported

confidence.rationale: The state manager already treats -1 as unknown brightness, but the observer previously never emitted that state after losing all active rows.

proposed_comments.title: Clarify that the mode follows supported built-in displays
proposed_comments.body:
### Clarify that the mode follows supported built-in displays

**Severity:** `medium`

The Settings description currently implies general display support, but the backend listens only to `WmiMonitorBrightness`, which is the built-in-display brightness path and does not cover ordinary external-monitor DDC/CI changes. Users on external-monitor-only systems could otherwise select a mode that silently receives no samples. Make the limitation explicit in the description.

```suggestion
    <value>Switch to light mode when built-in display brightness reaches this percentage, and to dark mode when it drops below it. Works with ambient light sensors and manual adjustments on supported built-in displays.</value>
```

confidence.rationale: The backend query is explicitly WmiMonitorBrightness and the changed resource text is user-facing.

proposed_comments.title: Add integration coverage for the new mode visibility and persistence
proposed_comments.body:
### Add integration coverage for the new mode visibility and persistence

**Severity:** `medium`

The added tests cover view-model cloning, clamping, and selection, but the Settings UI state and service interaction remain untested. Please add coverage that selects Follow Screen Brightness in Settings, verifies the threshold card appears, saves a non-default threshold, and exercises switching away from the mode so observer shutdown and stale-brightness invalidation stay covered.

confidence.rationale: The PR adds XAML state and service lifecycle behavior not covered by the current unit tests; exact UI-test plumbing is broader than a safe inline suggestion.
